reasons: The cited clause gives Customer a convenience right at one month's notice with no reciprocal IBM convenience right, which is at/above preferred on notice and mutuality, but conditions exit on early termination charges of unspecified, uncapped amount and provides no refund of prepaid fees. The fallback expressly permits an early-termination fee only 'not exceeding 3 months' fees', so an open-ended charge fails the fallback on a material term — a legitimate deviation rather than over-flagging.

The redline is additive and targeted: it appends a three-month aggregate cap and a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund to p0046 without disturbing the favourable one-month notice or the Customer right itself. This matches the redline guidance ('replace penalties with the fallback fee cap') and the model language's refund mechanic.

Deterministic flags are not substantive here: the 'Customer convenience termination present' regex looks at the edited paragraph (p0046) while the grant of the right sits in p0044, and the 0.661 changed-character ratio simply reflects appending a proviso to a very short sub-clause — no original wording was deleted.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, prefixed, states what changed and why, and correctly notes the notice period is already acceptable.
